title: TOPA — RB-47 ADVERSARIAL KILL PASS
motto: NOTHING SUPERNATURAL — ONLY NATURE NOT YET UNDERSTOOD.
mission: Attempt to destroy the remaining VISUAL <-> ELINT <-> GROUND_RADAR correlated-object interpretation using source-owner records, signal characteristics, geometry, instrument limits, chronology and contradictory contemporary documentation.
reason_for_demotion: The strongest extraordinary-looking element was the claimed three-way visual/ELINT/ground-radar correlation. A near-contemporaneous Duncanville/UTAH report explicitly states negative contact with the object, directly conflicting with the later/parallel Wing Intelligence summary that says UTAH confirmed, lost and reacquired a target. At the same time, much of the ELINT sequence is compatible in frequency, pulse characteristics and bearing with known terrestrial S-band radars. The surviving evidence therefore does not securely establish one physical source simultaneously producing the light, ELINT signal and ground-radar return.

attack_results.claim_attacked: Duncanville ground radar independently tracked the same object seen visually and detected by ELINT.
attack_results.evidence_for_claim: The 55th Strategic Reconnaissance Wing Intelligence summary states that after the crew supplied the estimated object position, ADC site UTAH immediately confirmed presence on its scopes, later lost contact, regained it during the turn, then lost it again.
attack_results.disconfirming_evidence: A formal Duncanville/UTAH teletype/report filed within hours states that the aircraft reported good contact while UTAH had negative contact with the object.
attack_results.topa_effect: Ground radar can no longer be treated as an uncontested O4 independent sensor leg. It becomes CONFLICTED_CONTEMPORARY_DOCUMENTATION.

attack_results.claim_attacked: The RB-47 itself actively radar-tracked the unknown object.
attack_results.evidence: Navigator Thomas Hanley later stated he searched with the navigation radar but never obtained radar contact; Chase's 1957 report also indicates unsuccessful airborne radar tracking. References in reports to airborne radar tracking are therefore most plausibly wording confusion with passive ECM/ELINT tracking.
attack_results.topa_effect: Remove AIRBORNE_ACTIVE_RADAR as a confirmed sensor channel.

attack_results.claim_attacked: The approximately 3 GHz signal requires an unknown airborne emitter associated with the visual object.

evidence.known_radar_overlap: AN/CPS-6B/FPS-10 vertical-center family includes approximately 2992-3019 MHz, similar microsecond pulse widths, 600 pps modes and rotation rates spanning the reported 4 rpm value. The ALA-6 was a passive direction finder designed to detect such radar emissions.

attack_results.topa_effect: The signal's fingerprint raises the terrestrial-radar prior rather than lowering it. This does not prove every ELINT event came from ground radar, but it removes the claim that the radio characteristics themselves are extraordinary.

attack_results.claim_attacked: Reported changing ELINT bearings cannot correspond to fixed ground radars.
attack_results.evidence: A detailed reconstruction using the surviving approximate track finds 1038Z-1040Z bearings compatible within stated multi-degree uncertainty with Duncanville and Oklahoma City S-band radar directions. After the Fort Worth turn, several later bearings point back toward Duncanville. McClure himself recalled being deluged with CPS-6B/FPS-10 signals in the Dallas-Fort Worth phase.
attack_results.limits: Exact navigation log is missing, heading/time errors are several degrees/minutes, and not every bearing is uniquely explained.
attack_results.topa_effect: ELINT-to-UFO association is weakened; multiple terrestrial emitters can reproduce a substantial portion of the bearing sequence.

attack_results.claim_attacked: The initial Mississippi up-scope signal proves an emitter circling the RB-47.
ordinary_models: Keesler CPS-6B emission plus intermittent ALA-6 relay/connection fault
later memory blending the early signal with Dallas-Fort Worth events
attack_results.support: A technician reportedly suggested a loose lead/relay-type fault after the flight; AN/ALA-6 specialists considered such relay failure technically plausible. Later descriptions of the early event are internally inconsistent about whether it only moved up-scope or continued around and down the other side.
attack_results.limit: No surviving raw scope recording exists to reproduce the anomaly.
attack_results.topa_effect: Not a HARD_SURVIVOR because missing raw data prevent a decisive instrument-level attack.

attack_results.claim_attacked: The 1010Z blue-white crossing light demonstrates extraordinary maneuvering.
attack_results.evidence: The object was a luminous point with no measured range, size or speed. Chase explicitly did not rule out a distant meteor when the possibility was later raised.
attack_results.topa_effect: Keep as unresolved visual testimony; do not use it to authenticate the later radio emitter.

attack_results.claim_attacked: Near-simultaneous visual disappearance, ELINT loss and ground-radar loss proves one extraordinary physical object.
reasons: The ground-radar channel is contradicted by UTAH's own near-contemporaneous negative-contact report.
The ELINT channel has strong terrestrial-radar candidates and no raw continuous recording publicly available.
The principal synchronization narrative comes through the Wing summary and later crew recollection, not three surviving independent raw sensor logs.
The on-board conversation recording is reported to begin only around 1048Z, after much of the earlier sequence; no public raw recording has been recovered.
attack_results.topa_effect: The case no longer satisfies HARD_SURVIVOR criteria based on causal sensor independence.

attack_results.claim_attacked: A large, bright, persistent object maneuvering around Dallas-Fort Worth should have produced independent external witnesses or additional radar reports.
attack_results.evidence: Available reconstructions note no comparable independent public ground-witness corpus and no secure multi-station air-defense radar confirmation despite other radar sites in the region.
attack_results.guard: Absence of a located report is not proof that no report existed.
attack_results.topa_effect: Lowers confidence in a large conspicuous craft model, but is not a decisive refutation.

what_still_survives: A real RB-47H crew reported unusual visual events and unusual passive electronic detections on 1957-07-17.
The case generated genuine military documentation and was not invented decades later.
The exact identity of the 1010Z visual light is not established.
The exact cause of the initial up-scope instrument anomaly is not established.
There is a real documentary contradiction over whether Duncanville/UTAH had a radar target corresponding to the crew's report.
No single demonstrated reconstruction currently proves every observation arose from one conventional source; however, the observations no longer require one common extraordinary source either.
what_did_not_survive: confirmed single physical object causing every observation
confirmed active airborne radar track from the RB-47
claim that approximately 3 GHz signal characteristics are alien/unique
claim that three independent raw sensor streams survive and synchronize exactly

next_killer_gates.test: Recover and compare the exact 745th ACWRON teletype, any earlier CIRVIS flash report, scope/operator logs and the Piwetz Wing summary. Determine whether 'negative contact' means no radar paint at all, no sustained/identifiable contact, or a later identification as ordinary traffic.

Search archival holdings for the reported ECM #3 wire recording or derivative transcript/magnetic copy beginning around 1048Z. If absent, permanently cap synchronization claims at documentary-summary level.
Propagate uncertainty in RB-47 position, heading, timing and ALA-6 bearing error against all known S-band emitters; quantify how often terrestrial radars reproduce the reported bearings by chance.

Recover Dallas-Fort Worth/Fort Worth area civil and military traffic, tower logs and possible searchlight-equipped aircraft activity for 1039-1058Z. Split the 1010Z Louisiana visual from the later Texas red-light sequence.

new_topa_laws: SENSOR_OWNER_RECORD outranks downstream narrative about that sensor unless the owner record is demonstrably incomplete or superseded.
A contradiction between contemporary records is evidence about uncertainty, not automatic evidence of cover-up.
A conventional explanation must survive the same attack as an extraordinary explanation, but a failed mundane candidate does not restore an extraordinary claim.
A case may remain historically unexplained while losing survivor status as evidence for extraordinary physics.

compact_result: TOPA succeeded in attacking its own strongest survivor. RB-47 remains a genuine, interesting and incompletely resolved 1957 military report, but the core 'three independent sensors tracked one object' claim is no longer secure because the sensor-owner record from Duncanville conflicts with the Wing summary, active airborne radar was not confirmed, and much of the passive ELINT sequence is compatible with terrestrial S-band radar geometry. The event survives; the extraordinary interpretation does not.
